easy.def: To try very hard or to stretch too far.
examples: I strain to lift it.
She strained her back.
He strained his eyes.

more.def: To use a lot of effort, or to hurt a muscle by stretching it too far.
examples: I strained to lift the heavy box.
She strained a muscle while running.
He strained to hear the faint sound.

easy.def: To pour water off through small holes.
examples: Strain the pasta.
Mom strained the soup.
Strain the juice.

more.def: To separate liquid from solids by pouring it through a sieve with small holes.
examples: Mom strained the pasta over the sink.
She strained the juice to remove the seeds.
Strain the soup before serving.

easy.def: Odd; not what you know.
examples: I heard a strange noise.
What a strange hat!
The food had a strange smell.

more.def: Unusual, odd, or not known to you.
examples: A strange light was blinking in the sky.
It felt strange to be at school at night.
The scientist found a strange new insect.

easy.def: In an odd way.
examples: The cat acted strangely.
It was strangely quiet.
He looked at me strangely.

more.def: In a way that is unusual or hard to explain.
examples: The cat acted strangely before the storm.
The house was strangely quiet.
The strangely shaped cloud looked like a hat.

easy.def: A person you do not know.
examples: Do not talk to a stranger.
A stranger asked the way.
The stranger waved.

more.def: A person that you have never met.
examples: A stranger asked us for directions.
I felt shy around the stranger.
The dog barked at the stranger.

easy.def: A strip of leather or cloth.
examples: My backpack has straps.
The strap broke.
The watch has a strap.

more.def: A long, narrow strip of cloth or leather used to carry or hold something.
examples: My backpack has two straps.
The strap of my sandal broke.
She tightened the strap on her watch.

easy.def: A plan to win or do something.
examples: Our strategy is to pass the ball.
The team has a strategy.
A good strategy helps.

more.def: A careful plan for reaching a goal, such as winning a game.
examples: Our team's strategy was to pass the ball.
She has a good strategy for chess.
The coach explained the strategy before the game.

easy.def: A thin tube for drinking.
examples: I drink with a straw.
The straw is red.
I put a straw in the cup.

more.def: A thin tube that you use to suck up a drink.
examples: I sipped juice through a straw.
The straw bent in the cup.
She put a straw in her milk.

easy.def: Dry yellow plant stems for animal beds.
examples: The barn has straw.
The cows sleep on straw.
The farmer stacked straw.

more.def: The dried stems of grain plants that are used for animal beds and for making hats.
examples: The horses slept on soft straw.
The farmer stacked straw in the barn.
She wore a hat made of straw.

easy.def: A small, red, sweet fruit with seeds on the outside.
examples: I eat a strawberry.
The strawberry is red.
Strawberries are sweet.

more.def: A small, red, juicy fruit with tiny seeds on its skin.
examples: I picked a ripe strawberry from the plant.
Mom put strawberries on the cereal.
Strawberry jam is sweet.

easy.def: Lost or wandering.
examples: A stray cat came by.
The stray dog was hungry.
We found a stray puppy.

more.def: Not belonging to anyone, or wandering away from home.
examples: A stray cat wandered into our yard.
The stray dog needed food and water.
We found a stray sock in the dryer.

easy.def: To wander away.
examples: Do not stray far.
The sheep strayed.
The child strayed from the group.

more.def: To wander away from where you should be.
examples: Do not stray from the path.
The sheep strayed from the flock.
The child strayed from her class.

easy.def: A long thin line or mark.
examples: There is a streak on the window.
The streak was red.
A streak of lightning.

more.def: A long, thin line or mark that is a different color from what is around it.
examples: A streak of mud ran down his leg.
A streak of light crossed the sky.
He had a gray streak in his hair.

easy.def: A string of wins.
examples: The team has a winning streak.
The streak ended.
A streak of good luck.

more.def: A series of similar events one after another.
examples: Our team is on a winning streak.
His streak of wins ended on Saturday.
She had a streak of good luck.

easy.def: A small river.
examples: We crossed a stream.
The stream is cold.
Fish swim in the stream.

more.def: A small, narrow river.
examples: We hopped over the stream.
The stream bubbled over the stones.
Trout swam in the cold stream.

easy.def: To flow in a steady line.
examples: Water streams down.
Tears streamed down her face.
Light streamed in.

more.def: To flow in a continuous line.
examples: Water streamed from the pipe.
Sunlight streamed through the window.
People streamed out of the stadium.

easy.def: A road in a town with houses.
examples: We live on a quiet street.
Cars drive down the street.
Look both ways before you cross the street.

more.def: A public road in a town or city, with houses or shops along it.
examples: The parade marched down the main street.
Our street has tall trees on both sides.
Shops and cafes lined the busy street.

easy.def: How strong you are.
examples: He has great strength.
Elephants have great strength.
I used all my strength.

more.def: The power to lift, push or do hard things.
examples: The weightlifter showed great strength.
Elephants have enormous strength.
She used all her strength to open the jar.

easy.def: A worried or tense feeling.
examples: Too much homework causes stress.
Exercise can ease stress.
She felt stress before the test.

more.def: A feeling of being worried or tense because of too much to do or think about.
examples: Taking a walk can lower your stress.
A big test can cause stress for some students.
Deep breaths helped him cope with stress.

easy.def: Extra push on part of a word when you say it.
examples: The stress in "table" is on the first part.
Say the word with stress on the first syllable.
The stress is on "pen" in "pencil."

more.def: The extra force you put on one part of a word when you say it.
examples: The stress in the word "table" falls on the first syllable.
Dictionaries show where the stress goes in each word.
Put the stress on the second part of "begin."

easy.def: To make something longer or wider.
examples: I stretch the rubber band.
She stretched her arms.
The cat stretched.

more.def: To pull something so that it gets longer, or to reach out your body to its full length.
examples: The cat stretched on the rug.
He stretched the rubber band until it was thin.
She stretched her arms above her head.

easy.def: A long piece of land or time.
examples: The road has a long stretch of straight.
A stretch of sand is by the sea.
It was a long stretch of days.

more.def: A long, unbroken piece of land, road or time.
examples: A stretch of sandy beach lay along the coast.
The road has a long, straight stretch.
It was a long stretch without any rain.

easy.def: Making sure rules are followed.
examples: The teacher is strict.
We have a strict rule.
A strict coach.

more.def: Firm in making sure that rules are obeyed.
examples: The teacher is strict about homework.
We have a strict rule about running in the halls.
The coach was strict but fair.

easy.def: Firmly.
examples: Running is strictly not allowed.
The rule is strictly followed.
It is strictly forbidden.

more.def: In a strict way, or only.
examples: Running in the hall is strictly forbidden.
The rule was strictly followed.
This room is strictly for staff.

easy.def: To hit something hard.
examples: Lightning can strike a tree.
A rock struck the wall.
He struck the drum.

more.def: To hit something with force.
examples: Lightning struck the old oak tree.
The ball struck the window.
She struck the match to light the candle.

easy.def: A miss in baseball.
examples: He swung and got a strike.
Three strikes and you are out.
The pitcher threw a strike.

more.def: In baseball, a pitch that the batter swings at and misses, or that crosses the plate without a swing.
examples: The pitcher threw a fast strike over the plate.
Three strikes and the batter is out.
She swung and missed for strike two.

easy.def: A thin cord.
examples: I tied a string around the box.
The kite has a string.
The string is long.

more.def: A thin cord made of twisted threads, used for tying things.
examples: She wound the string tightly around the spool.
The kite flew on a long string.
The guitar has six strings.

easy.def: The musicians who play violins and cellos.
examples: The strings play softly.
The strings are in the back.
I play in the strings.

more.def: The group of players in an orchestra who play violins, cellos and similar instruments.
examples: The strings began the piece softly.
She plays cello in the strings.
The strings sat to the left of the stage.

easy.def: A long, thin piece of something.
examples: I cut a strip of paper.
A strip of cloth was tied around it.
He ate a strip of bacon.

more.def: A long, narrow piece of paper, cloth or other material.
examples: She cut a strip of paper for the bookmark.
A strip of tape held the box shut.
He tied a strip of cloth around the post.

easy.def: A long, narrow band of color.
examples: The zebra has stripes.
My shirt has a blue stripe.
The flag has stripes.

more.def: A long, narrow band that is a different color from what is around it.
examples: The zebra has black and white stripes.
My shirt has a red stripe.
The flag has thirteen stripes.

easy.def: To rub gently with your hand.
examples: She stroked the cat.
I stroke the dog.
He stroked the horse.

more.def: To move your hand gently over something again and again.
examples: She stroked the cat's soft fur.
He stroked the horse's neck.
Mom stroked my hair.

easy.def: One movement of a pen, brush or arm.
examples: One stroke of the brush.
The swimmer takes a stroke.
The artist made a stroke.

more.def: A single movement of a brush, pen or arm, or one way of swimming.
examples: The artist painted with long strokes of the brush.
The swimmer took a strong stroke.
The backstroke is my favorite swimming stroke.

easy.def: To walk in a slow, easy way.
examples: We stroll in the park.
She strolled by the lake.
They strolled home.

more.def: To walk slowly for pleasure, not in a hurry.
examples: We strolled through the park after dinner.
She strolled along the beach.
They strolled home in the sunshine.

easy.def: Having a lot of power.
examples: The strong man lifted the box.
An ox is strong.
The rope is strong.

more.def: Having great strength or power, and not easy to break.
examples: The strong wind blew down a branch.
She is strong enough to carry the heavy bag.
The bridge is built of strong steel.

easy.def: Easy to notice.
examples: There was a strong smell.
The tea is strong.
The sun is strong today.

more.def: Easy to notice, with a lot of flavor, smell or force.
examples: The strong smell of onions filled the kitchen.
The tea was too strong for me.
A strong wind blew across the field.

easy.def: In a powerful way.
examples: He pushed strongly.
I strongly believe it.
The wind blew strongly.

more.def: In a way that is powerful or firm.
examples: He pushed strongly on the door.
I strongly believe that you are right.
The wind blew strongly all day.

easy.def: Something that is built.
examples: The tower is a tall structure.
The bridge is a strong structure.
The structure is old.

more.def: Something that has been built, such as a building or a bridge.
examples: The Eiffel Tower is a tall structure.
The old bridge is a sturdy structure.
The bird built a neat structure out of twigs.

easy.def: The way the parts of something are put together.
examples: The structure of a leaf is thin.
The structure of the story was clear.
The body has a structure.

more.def: The way that the parts of something are arranged.
examples: The structure of a leaf helps it catch sunlight.
The story has a simple structure with three parts.
Scientists study the structure of the body.

easy.def: To try very hard to do something that is difficult.
examples: I struggle to lift the box.
She struggled to open the jar.
The ant struggled with the crumb.

more.def: To try hard to do something that is difficult or to get free.
examples: He struggled to carry all the bags.
The little bird struggled to get out of the net.
Some students struggle with math until they practice more.

easy.def: A hard try.
examples: It was a struggle to get up.
The long walk was a struggle.
Learning to read was a struggle.

more.def: A hard effort to do something difficult, or a long fight against a problem.
examples: Climbing the steep hill was a struggle.
It was a struggle to stay awake.
Their struggle for clean water lasted many years.

easy.def: Not wanting to change your mind.
examples: The stubborn puppy would not come inside.
My stubborn dog will not take a bath.
Do not be stubborn. Try the peas.

more.def: Refusing to change your mind or do what others want.
examples: He was too stubborn to admit that he was lost.
The stubborn stain would not come out.
The stubborn mule refused to cross the bridge.

easy.def: A person who goes to school.
examples: The student reads a book.
Each student has a desk.
A new student joined our class.

more.def: A person who is learning at a school or college.
examples: Every student received a new notebook.
The student raised her hand.
The new student sat by the window.

easy.def: A room where an artist works.
examples: The painter has a studio.
The studio is full of paint.
She works in her studio.

more.def: A room or building where an artist, musician or photographer works, or where movies and shows are made.
examples: The artist painted in a bright studio with big windows.
The band recorded its songs in a music studio.
The photographer set up lights in her studio.

easy.def: To learn by reading and thinking.
examples: I study for my test.
She studies math.
We studied frogs.

more.def: To spend time learning about something by reading and thinking.
examples: I study my spelling words every night.
Scientists study the stars with telescopes.
She studied maps to plan the trip.

easy.def: Learning about something with care.
examples: The study of space is fun.
Scientists did a study of bees.
Her study took an hour.

more.def: A careful look at something to learn about it.
examples: The scientists published a study about bees.
A study of birds showed that many fly south.
Her study of the volcano took three years.

related.def: Spending a lot of time studying.

easy.def: Things that you do not name.
examples: I packed my stuff.
Put your stuff away.
There is stuff in the box.

more.def: Things or materials that are not named exactly.
examples: Put all your stuff in your backpack before you leave.
What is that sticky stuff on the table?
There is a lot of old stuff in the attic.

easy.def: To trip and almost fall.
examples: I stumbled on a rock.
She stumbled over the toy.
He stumbled on the stairs.

more.def: To trip over something and nearly fall.
examples: I stumbled over a rock on the trail.
She stumbled on the stairs but caught the rail.
He stumbled in the dark.

easy.def: A dangerous or tricky act.
examples: The stunt was amazing.
He did a stunt on his bike.
A stunt performer jumped.

more.def: A difficult or daring act that is done to show skill or to be exciting.
examples: The rider did a stunt on his bike.
A stunt performer jumped over the cars in the movie.
The circus had a stunt with a flying trapeze.

easy.def: Not showing good thinking.
examples: Leaving the door open was a stupid thing to do.
That was a stupid mistake.
I felt stupid when I forgot my own name.

more.def: Showing poor thinking or a lack of common sense.
examples: It was a stupid mistake to leave the gate open, and the sheep got out.
Running into the street without looking is a stupid thing to do.
He felt stupid after locking his keys inside the car.

easy.def: A way of doing something.
examples: I like her style.
He writes in a funny style.
The house has a modern style.

more.def: A particular way of doing, making or looking.
examples: I like her style of dressing.
The author writes in a funny style.
The house is built in an old-fashioned style.
